stated_purpose: Announce his candidacy for the Senate seat vacated by Gary Peters
observable_function: Launch interview with Semafor plus an endorsement from Bernie Sanders
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The launch was framed as a progressive challenge to the party establishment rather than as a general-election debut; the endorsement was the news peg, not the event itself.

speech_summary: Launch interview: Trump and Musk "are going to leave a lot of wreckage in their wake".

event_title: Petition filing for the Democratic primary ballot
stated_purpose: File nominating petitions to appear on the August 4 primary ballot
observable_function: Bureau of Elections candidate listing records El-Sayed as a Democratic candidate nominated by petitions on 04/14/2026
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Filing was a procedural gate; the official listing date is the most reliable date in the whole schedule.
main_messages: unknown

stated_purpose: Meet voters on a university campus during the primary campaign
observable_function: Documented by a photographer as 'US Senate candidate for Michigan Abdul El-Sayed meets voters at Michigan Technological University'
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: One of the few campaign stops in the Upper Peninsula captured in a licensed photograph, consistent with the primary strategy of touring college campuses.
main_messages: unknown

event_title: Democratic primary forum hosted by the United Auto Workers
stated_purpose: First multi-candidate Democratic primary forum
observable_function: All three then-active Democratic candidates participated; moderated by Mark DePaoli, Brandon Mancilla and LaShawn English
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: A labor-hosted forum put wage and manufacturing questions at the centre of the primary before the campaign's Israel argument took over.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: Recorded in the Wikipedia debate table with a YouTube link; the video page was not retrieved.

event_title: Forum hosted by the Council of Baptist Pastors of Detroit and Vicinity
stated_purpose: Primary forum on voting rights and healthcare before Black church audiences
observable_function: Three-candidate forum moderated by Jackie Nelson and James Williams
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The setting made Black church congregations the audience, an electorate El-Sayed ultimately lost in Detroit.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: Host organisation's name places it in Detroit; the exact venue was not reported in retrieved sources.

stated_purpose: Policy-focused debate on the final evening of the conference
observable_function: Widely televised and streamed debate moderated by Nolan Finley and Stephen Henderson; AI data centres and AIPAC funding dominated
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The most policy-dense forum of the primary, and the one where El-Sayed's data-centre position first got extended airtime.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: The conference was described as a closed-door event for politicians, business leaders and media, televised and streamed by the chamber.

stated_purpose: First head-to-head debate after McMorrow's withdrawal
observable_function: Televised hour-long debate moderated by Rick Albin; rivals split on Medicare for All, ICE and Israel policy
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: With the field down to two, the debate converted a three-way argument into a straight establishment-versus-insurgent contrast.
main_messages: Medicare for All, abolish ICE, end unconditional aid to Israel, no PAC money
speech_summary: El-Sayed framed affordability around Medicare for All, monopolies, wages and 'getting the corruption out of our politics'.
analyst_notes: Venue and moderator from the Wikipedia debate table; the on-site report places the debate in Grand Rapids.

stated_purpose: Canvassing with volunteers on primary day-week
observable_function: El-Sayed spoke to volunteers during a canvassing event, photographed by CNN
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Same day as the WOOD-TV8 debate, showing the campaign paired televised appearances with volunteer canvasses.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: Documented only by a photo caption in the CNN report on the Obama-footage ad.

event_title: Fox 2 Detroit final Democratic primary debate
stated_purpose: Final primary debate one week before election day
observable_function: Aired as a special edition of 'The Pulse', moderated by Roop Raj; transparency and campaign finance dominated
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The debate shifted the closing week's agenda from policy to disclosure, an issue on which El-Sayed had been on the defensive for weeks.
main_messages: Release of financial disclosure, outside spending, DTE Energy donations
analyst_notes: El-Sayed released his financial disclosure just before the debate; net worth reported as up to $2.1 million.

stated_purpose: Gather supporters while primary votes were counted
observable_function: Watch party attended by supporters and covered by Bridge Michigan; El-Sayed spoke before the race was called
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The venue choice kept the campaign in Detroit even though it lost Wayne County, signalling where its coalition needed to grow.
main_messages: "...built on the foundation of what this government was supposed to be in the first place, government of the people, by the people."
speech_summary: Thanked supporters and framed the campaign as a movement.
analyst_notes: Race called by AP at 9:56 a.m. the next morning; El-Sayed spoke earlier that morning.

event_title: Post-primary news conference at the Spirit of Detroit
stated_purpose: Speak to press after being declared the Democratic nominee
observable_function: News conference with McMorrow present, photographed for the AP and Bridge Michigan
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: McMorrow's appearance beside him was the visual proof of party consolidation after a divisive primary.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: Known from a photo caption; no transcript of the news conference was retrieved.

stated_purpose: First general-election debate of the cycle
observable_function: El-Sayed appeared alone after Rogers' team declined the invitation that morning; Fox 2 kept an empty podium
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: A one-candidate debate let El-Sayed define Rogers unchallenged on Medicare for All, Israel and the Iran war for an hour of local television.
main_messages: Medicare for All, Israel-Palestine, the Iran war, Hasan Piker
visual_notes: An empty podium was placed for Rogers.
analyst_notes: Video URL from the Wikipedia debate table; the page itself was not retrieved.

stated_purpose: First face-to-face debate of the general election
observable_function: Hour-long debate moderated by Rick Albin covering gas prices, tariffs, immigration, the Iran war, Israel and surveillance
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The debate quickly became personal — wealth, campaign funding and records — rather than a policy comparison.
main_messages: Trump's tariffs are 'chaotic... ham-fisted'; Rogers is a 'sock puppet'
analyst_notes: Rogers used the debate to say he would accept AIPAC help, which preceded a UDP mailer the next day.

stated_purpose: Campaign stop in west Michigan
observable_function: Event was disrupted by agitators, per MLive
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Records a disruption without establishing who the agitators were or what they said; the retrieved report does not identify them.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: Headline-level record; the city and venue are not in the retrieved text.

stated_purpose: Policy forum with both general-election nominees
observable_function: Both candidates answered detailed questions on tariffs, AI and the auto industry
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The only retrieved event where the two nominees discussed industrial policy at length rather than trading attacks.
main_messages: Trump's tariffs hurt the auto industry; build a $25,000 300-mile EV; tariff the EV market to incubate domestic production
speech_summary: Tariffs compared to chemotherapy: 'You don't give all the chemo all at once.'
analyst_notes: Moderated by Jason Colthorp per the Wikipedia debate table.

stated_purpose: Final televised debate before election day
observable_function: Debate moderated by Chuck Stokes, Carolyn Clifford and Alicia Smith; Iran, trust and Trump dominated
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The closing debate put the Iran war and Rogers' ties to Trump at the centre, the two themes El-Sayed used in his final ads and speeches.
main_messages: Rogers is 'a sock puppet for the man'; Iran's threat 'had been contained' by the nuclear deal
analyst_notes: Moderators from the Wikipedia debate table; CBS report confirms the debate and quotes.

event_title: Rally with former President Barack Obama
stated_purpose: Turnout rally with the former president in the campaign's final week
observable_function: Obama praised El-Sayed's money-in-politics and healthcare proposals and attacked Trump
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The rally supplied the campaign's highest-profile national validation after the primary, in the metro area where El-Sayed was weakest.
main_messages: "Trump is using the presidency to enrich himself and his family." (Obama)
analyst_notes: Date and city from El-Sayed's Wikipedia biography; no independently retrieved news report of the rally (the Politico preview returned HTTP 403).

stated_purpose: Declare victory after the race was called
observable_function: El-Sayed addressed supporters in Detroit at about 2:27 a.m. after the AP called the race; attendees chanted 'Free Palestine'
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The speech joined a unifying 'I love America' message with an explicit restatement of his Israel position, refusing to choose between the two.
main_messages: "We just showed them that a movement of the people, by the people, and for the people will ultimately win."
speech_summary: Claimed the win as a movement victory, restated his position on U.S. money and Israel.
analyst_notes: Attendance figures were not reported; Mahmoud Khalil's presence is recorded in the Wikipedia biography.

event_title: Launch of second U.S. Senate campaign
stated_purpose: Announce a second Senate bid for the seat vacated by Gary Peters
observable_function: Announcement reported nationally; Semafor recorded that he announced 'this week'
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Rogers entered as the consolidating establishment favourite, unlike his 2024 primary; the launch was designed to signal that the party had settled on him.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: The Detroit Free Press launch story returned HTTP 402 (paywall), so the announcement's venue and text were not retrievable.

event_title: Petition filing for the Republican primary ballot
stated_purpose: File nominating petitions for the August 4 primary
observable_function: Bureau of Elections candidate listing records Rogers as a Republican candidate nominated by petitions on 04/17/2026
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Filing came three days after El-Sayed's, with no contested primary on the Republican side.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: Official filing date from the Bureau of Elections candidate listing.

stated_purpose: Announce an outreach effort to Democratic-leaning voters
observable_function: Rogers appeared with a group of Democratic-leaning voters and spoke at a podium
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The effort targeted the Democratic primary's losers directly, two weeks after El-Sayed's narrow win and before Stevens' endorsement.
main_messages: "I'm not asking you to be a Republican. I'm asking you for the opportunity to earn your trust."
speech_summary: Asked Democratic voters for their trust and promised to represent everybody.
analyst_notes: Photograph caption dates the launch Aug 20, 2026 in Detroit.

event_title: Declined invitation to the Fox 2 Detroit debate
stated_purpose: Candidate invitation to the first general-election debate
observable_function: Rogers' team declined the invitation on the morning of the debate; El-Sayed appeared alone
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The first declination set a pattern of one joint and three single-candidate or later debates, and let El-Sayed hold an hour of television unanswered.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: Recorded as cancelled because the invited candidate did not attend; the broadcast itself went ahead with one candidate.

stated_purpose: Roll out a slate of business-group endorsements
observable_function: Campaign announced endorsements from business groups and used them to argue Rogers would protect jobs
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The endorsements were announced, not staged as a public event; the archive records the announcement, not a rally.
main_messages: "The house is on fire. And we can't sit back as it rages on."
speech_summary: Rogers promised to 'get kids reading at grade level again'.
analyst_notes: event_status=announced: a written endorsement announcement, with no public venue retrieved.

event_title: Proposal to pause Michigan's gas tax
stated_purpose: Propose a state gas tax holiday
observable_function: Written proposal released to press; a Republican legislative leader rejected it the same day
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The proposal was aimed at the affordability message El-Sayed owned, but it split Rogers from his own party's legislative record.
main_messages: The 2019 gas tax increase from 31 to 51 cents was 'unconscionable'.
analyst_notes: Recorded as an announcement; no public event with a venue was retrieved.

event_title: 'Barn party' campaign rally with Sen. John Kennedy
stated_purpose: Rally with an out-of-state Senate surrogate
observable_function: Kennedy touted Rogers' House and Intelligence Committee record; Rogers took press questions
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Importing a Southern senator signalled that Rogers' coalition-building ran through national conservative media figures rather than Michigan officeholders.
target_audience: Republican base voters in Oakland County
main_messages: "They don't let just anybody be the chairman of the Intelligence Committee." (Kennedy)
visual_notes: Photograph shows Rogers and Kennedy speaking to reporters outdoors.
analyst_notes: Article published Oct 14, 2026; the event is dated Friday Oct 9, 2026 in the caption and text.

stated_purpose: First face-to-face debate of the general election
observable_function: Rogers debated El-Sayed on gas prices, tariffs, immigration, Iran and Israel
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Rogers used the debate to accept AIPAC support publicly, reversing his August request that AIPAC stay out.
main_messages: "We can't afford Abdul"; "Anybody that wants to help my campaign ... I'll take all of that help."
analyst_notes: The AIPAC answer is quoted by The American Prospect from the same debate.

stated_purpose: Policy forum with both nominees
observable_function: Rogers answered questions on tariffs, Canada, AI and the auto industry
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Rogers defended tariffs as correcting '40 years of bad trade policy' while asking for adjustments, keeping both the Trump base and Michigan manufacturers in view.
main_messages: Tariffs corrected decades of bad trade policy; Canada trade war should end; federal AI guardrails needed
analyst_notes: Rogers cited GM moving Silverado production to the Orion plant as evidence tariffs worked.

stated_purpose: Final televised debate before election day
observable_function: Rogers attacked El-Sayed's trustworthiness and association with Hasan Piker; questioned whether El-Sayed could get a security clearance
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Rogers closed on character and security rather than policy, the inverse of El-Sayed's closing frame.
main_messages: "You'll be lucky to have a damn pair of pants when you're done."
analyst_notes: Rogers told reporters afterwards he questions whether El-Sayed can get a security clearance.

stated_purpose: Announce a trade-association PAC endorsement
observable_function: AGC PAC announced its endorsement in a press release
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Construction-industry endorsements reinforced the infrastructure-and-jobs message in the campaign's final two weeks.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: event_status=announced: endorsement announcement only; no venue.

event_title: Trump rally at McMorran Place Arena (Nicki Minaj appearance)
stated_purpose: National surrogate rally for Michigan Republicans
observable_function: Trump headlined; Nicki Minaj urged the crowd to support Rogers and John James
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The rally put Rogers' name in a national spectacle without requiring him to share a stage with the President's most controversial lines.
main_messages: Minaj: "Since he's come back, he's changed the energy of our country."
analyst_notes: The retrieved report does not state whether Rogers personally attended; it records Minaj urging support for him.

stated_purpose: Raise money with AIPAC-connected donors
observable_function: Attendance at four AIPAC-hosted fundraisers in August 2026 (recorded in the Wikipedia biography, which cites reporting)
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The fundraisers are the clearest evidence that Rogers' August request that AIPAC stay out of the race did not extend to its money.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: No exact date retrieved. Wikipedia says four fundraisers; The American Prospect says three, hosted the day after Rogers met AIPAC's board chair. The count conflicts.

stated_purpose: Respond publicly to the result
observable_function: Rogers released a written statement thanking supporters; it did not explicitly concede
analyst_interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The non-concession statement kept a fourth statewide race open without contradicting the result.
main_messages: unknown
analyst_notes: Written statement, not a public event; no venue. Sources disagree on whether it amounted to a concession.
